label: <DEL> in length-3 sequences (esp. starting m/v/h/1/3) OR "e"/"o" right after a leading "l"
predicate: ((phase == 1) & (L == 3) & isin(first_tok, [tok("m"), tok("v"), tok("h"), tok("1"), tok("3")])) | ((t == 1) & (prev_tok == tok("l")) & isin(in_tok, [tok("e"), tok("o")]))
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (~0.03% of steps) with two unrelated components. (1) Delimiter step of L=3 sequences (about 50% of activation mass, and all the largest activations): fires on <DEL> when the sequence is only 3 tokens long, mostly when the first token is m, v, h, 1 or 3 (top examples: m i l, v l l, m 3 s, m s l). Even with that restriction most such delimiters stay silent, so which ones fire depends on the token identities in a way no simple rule captures. Rarely it also fires on <DEL> at L=4. (2) Original phase at t=1 when the sequence starts with l and the second token is e or o (le..., lo...): 100% precision, about 37% of mass, small and nearly constant magnitude (~0.08-0.10 of max). A weaker version shows up at t=2 after l (3 l e, 3 l n). Basically never fires in the copy phase (just a few steps on the first copied token after <DEL> when L=3) and never at t=0 or t>=5. Magnitude is largest for the L=3 delimiter component.
